videos.video_subject: Cristiano Ronaldo's career story from Madeira to Manchester United, Real Madrid, Portugal's Euro 2016 win and Al Nassr, and the chase for 1,000 career goals
videos.video_script: Cristiano Ronaldo was never supposed to be the greatest. He was a skinny kid from Madeira, who left home at twelve with nothing but a bag and a promise to himself. At eighteen, Alex Ferguson handed him the number seven at Manchester United, and a teenager who needed a push became a machine nobody could stop. Then came Real Madrid. Nine years. Four hundred and fifty goals, more than any player in the history of the club, and the Champions League lifted again and again. Five Ballon d'Ors. Three leagues in three different countries. And for Portugal, the one trophy that mattered most. Euro twenty sixteen, the final, tears on the touchline when injury took him off, and then a nation winning without him in the pitch, and with him in every heartbeat. Everyone said he was finished when he left Europe for Saudi Arabia. Instead, he kept scoring. He kept training harder than players half his age. He became the top scorer in international football history, and then passed nine hundred career goals, a number no one had ever reached. He is past forty now, and the legs of every defender who ever faced him are long retired. People still ask when it ends. He never answers. Because Ronaldo has never played for the applause, he plays for the next record. The next goal. The next doubt to silence. So the only question left is simple. Can he really reach one thousand goals?
